memory_candidates.content: Sapience's ~/.sapience/config.json is owner-only state (mode 600, self-updating daily) that no agent may edit directly. When a task's measurement or decision depends on a prior task's owner-action reconciliation of this file, verify the live file's actual contents at dispatch time rather than trusting the prior task's [COMPLETED] status alone -- a task can correctly complete by drafting and rehearsing an owner instruction without that instruction ever having been run.

sapience coverage's two skip filters (headless/agent vs. subagent/harness-started) can diverge sharply on an orchestration-heavy workflow: a live read showed 30 headless/agent skips vs. 874 subagent/harness-started skips out of 1120 available session files, a roughly 29x gap, even under a stale pre-reconciliation folder set. Worth re-checking whether this ratio persists once the capture population changes.
